question: Where does nutpie's per-gradient lead over oWALNUTS on the fixed 16 (WP76: oWALNUTS/nutpie (c) 0.699, a 1.43x nutpie lead) come from, model by model and mechanism by mechanism? WP71 (nutpie's metric estimator) and WP73 (warmup spend) are ruled out as sufficient explanations.
output: A ranked list of mechanisms with evidence. No candidate sampler change, no default change, no flag.

commit.note: WP72's commit under test (default sampler identical to f097391c)

part1.what: descriptive decomposition from the 288 + 288 fixed-16 cells already on disk; no new cell
part1.owalnuts_cells: WP64 posteriordb_bench_v7_linux_v1/artifacts/{v7,ext}/cells (560561-3 at f097391c, 620601-3 at c5c60122) and WP72 posteriordb_ratio_robustness_v1/artifacts/cells (720701-12 at c5c60122)
part1.split: per paired seed (both cells status ok): G = ln(nutpie min-bulk-ESS per gradient / oWALNUTS) = A + B + C exactly; A = ln(min bulk ESS n/o) (ESS per draw; both arms retain 4 x 1,000); B = ln(sampling gradients o/n) (sampling gradients per retained draw); C = ln((total/sampling gradients) o / (total/sampling) n) (warmup overhead). Per model: mean over paired ok seeds; a model enters with >= 15 of 18 paired ok seeds (WP72 rule). Carrying = largest mean G. Also reported: WP76's per-model (c), each model's share of the sum of G, and the cell-level approximation ln(gradients_sampling / retained_leaves_built) of the oWALNUTS refinement spend.

telemetry.design: 4 chains x 1,000 warmup / 1,000 retained, both samplers, v7 cell code. oWALNUTS: the 'telemetry' binary = v7's main.rs plus per-transition arrays (retained and warmup) of depth, target_evaluations, leaves_attempted, leaves_built, refinement_attempts, selected_refinement_level, step_size, maximum_absolute_energy_error, orbit_states, reverse_coarser_rejections, divergent, acceptance_statistic, stop; with the final mass diagonal and step size per chain. nutpie: nutpie.sample(..., store_mass_matrix=True, store_unconstrained=True), every numeric sample_stats variable kept (step_size, depth, n_steps, diverging, mean_tree_accept, mass_matrix_inv, unconstrained_draw, ...), retained and warmup. Storage only: no sampler setting changes.
telemetry.seed_reuse: seeds 720701-3 are WP72's / WP76's, so each telemetry cell is checked against the same-seed prior cell (status, gradients_total, gradients_sampling, min_bulk_ess, divergences equal); a mismatch is reported, not repaired
telemetry.run_order: models in the order listed, oWALNUTS then nutpie, seeds ascending; one child process per cell; strictly sequential; no reruns

platform.machine: AWS EC2 c7a.4xlarge (AMD EPYC 9R14), Ubuntu 24.04, lane 1: taskset -c 0-3, RAYON_NUM_THREADS=4, OMP_NUM_THREADS=1, files under ~/lanes/nutpie_gap_decomposition_v1/
platform.wall_label_note: Linux, core-pinned to 4 dedicated cores (taskset -c 0-3) on a shared box with other pinned lanes active (shared L3 and memory bandwidth): walls are 'pinned, co-tenanted'. Pass counts, gradient counts and ESS per gradient are unaffected by co-tenancy. No statistic of this study uses a wall.
platform.software: lane venv on Python 3.12.3: nutpie 0.16.8, bridgestan 2.9.0, arviz 0.23.4, numpy 2.4.6, scipy 1.17.1, xarray 2026.9.0, posteriordb 0.2.0, pandas 3.1.0, cmdstanpy 1.3.0; oWALNUTS harness built with Rust 1.88.0 on the box (as WP64/WP72), --release --locked -j4

analysis.telemetry_split: per usable telemetry seed (both cells status ok), with sums over the 4 x 1,000 retained transitions: B = ln(sum oWALNUTS target_evaluations / sum nutpie n_steps) = B4 + B1 + B2 exactly. B4 = ln(sum target_evaluations / sum leaves_attempted) (gradients per attempted macro leaf: refinement micro-steps and reverse checks; nutpie's equivalent is 1). B1 = ln(e_n / e_o), ln e = mean over chains of the median over unconstrained coordinates i of ln(eps * sqrt(Minv_i) / sigma_i). B2 = B - B4 - B1 = ln((leaves attempted per draw x e_o) / (n_steps per draw x e_n)), the distance per draw in posterior-scale units. Per model: mean over usable seeds.
analysis.metric_conventions: oWALNUTS: mass_diagonal is M with K(p) = 0.5 sum p_i^2 / M_i (src/walnutpie.rs module docs), so Minv_i = 1 / M_i; eps = final_step_size (the retained macro step). nutpie: Minv = mass_matrix_inv at the last retained draw (fixed after tuning); eps = step_size at the last retained draw.
analysis.sigma: sigma_i = 1.4826 x MAD of coordinate i over the pooled unconstrained retained draws of both samplers of that seed (8,000 draws); the sd where the MAD is 0
analysis.H3_spread: S = mean over chains of the SD over coordinates of ln(Minv_i / sigma_i^2) (the overall level is absorbed by the step and is reported only)
analysis.ranking: the five additive components A (ESS per draw), C (warmup), B4 (refinement spend), B1 (step), B2 (distance per draw), ranked by their mean over the three carrying models on the telemetry seeds; H3 is a cause test for B1 and is reported beside it, not ranked as an additive term

H1_step.mechanism: oWALNUTS adapts a smaller effective step than nutpie, so each draw needs more leapfrog steps for the same distance
H1_step.criterion: B1 >= ln 1.25 on >= 2 of the 3 carrying models

H2_distance_per_draw.mechanism: oWALNUTS travels further per draw (longer orbits: U-turn criterion, depth, unmerged final subtrees) than nutpie at its own step
H2_distance_per_draw.diagnostic: B2, with the depth and n_steps distributions and the unmerged-leaf fraction
H2_distance_per_draw.criterion: B2 >= ln 1.25 on >= 2 of the 3 carrying models

H3_metric_match.mechanism: oWALNUTS's final diagonal metric matches the posterior scales worse than nutpie's, which forces its smaller step
H3_metric_match.criterion: S_o - S_n >= 0.35 on >= 2 of the 3 carrying models

H4_refinement_spend.mechanism: oWALNUTS spends gradients on step-size refinement and reverse checks that nutpie does not
H4_refinement_spend.criterion: B4 >= ln 1.25 on >= 2 of the 3 carrying models

H5_ess_per_draw.mechanism: at the same number of draws, oWALNUTS's draws are less independent (lower min bulk ESS per draw)
H5_ess_per_draw.criterion: A >= ln 1.25 on >= 2 of the 3 carrying models

P1.text: the three models with the largest mean G in part 1 are sblrc-blr, hmm_drive_0 and eight_schools_centered (WP76's three lowest per-model (c): 0.342, 0.484, 0.607; accel_gp at 0.610 is the nearest rival)

P2.text: the first-ranked component is B1 (step size): WP71 and WP73 ruled out the metric estimator and warmup spend, leaving the adapted step given the metric

P3.text: on diamonds (where oWALNUTS leads) B1 is below ln 1.25

rules: Freeze PREREGISTRATION.md and protocol.json in a commit before the first telemetry cell and before part 1 is computed. Sequential cells; failures, crashes and timeouts are results; no reruns, no tuning after results. A driver crash may be relaunched; only an interrupted cell without a completed artifact may be rerun from scratch with the same seed, recorded in AMENDMENTS.md. Raw draws and telemetry are checksummed and not committed.
